committed_on: 2026-10-27, before any C2 session was generated or scored
attacker: White-box: it knows the trained detector (LightGBM, configs/sim_v3.json, fitted and calibrated on sim_fa2 train and calibration splits exactly as for the gate test), its alarm threshold and persistence rule. For each simulated world it tries every value on a fixed grid of its one free parameter and keeps the largest one that the detector does not alarm on after onset.

ramp.cost: final position offset = rate x (60 s - 20 s onset)

consistent_takeover.cost: final position offset from the takeover profile (acceleration for accel_s, then constant velocity)

variants: default attacker (C/N0 raised, geometry as sampled)
worlds: 150 per family per variant, seeds from numpy SeedSequence(777), onset fixed at 20 s, duration 60 s, 10 Hz; a world is one simulated trajectory/noise realisation; the same world is used for every grid value
measures: detection rate at each fixed grid value (non-adaptive curve)
adaptive success: share of worlds in which the attacker finds an undetected value, and the share reaching an undetected final offset of at least 25 m, 50 m, 100 m (100 m only if the grid allows it)
alarms before onset are not counted as detections
reported_as: worst case over the attacker's search, side by side with the non-adaptive detection numbers of the gate test (sim_test5) and C1 (sim_default1, sim_matched1)
no_retuning: the detector is not changed; if it is hardened against this attacker later, that is a separate logged change tested on a new set
limits: one free parameter per family, a fixed grid and white-box access; a stronger attacker (more parameters, a finer search, joint power and path optimisation) could do better, so these numbers are a lower bound on the worst case
